When multiple skills apply, process skills come first — they set the approach, then implementation skills (frontend-design, etc.) carry it out. Brainstorming and systematic-debugging are Superpowers' most common process skills, but the rule holds for any of them.

- "Let's build X" → superpowers:brainstorming first, then implementation skills.

[project]
name = "gqa-flash-autoresearch"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "Autoresearch loop for a Triton GQA flash-attention kernel on RTX 5090"
requires-python = ">=3.12,<3.13"
dependencies = [
    "torch",
    "numpy",
    "matplotlib",
    "pytest",
    "flash-attn==2.8.3.post2",
    # flash-attn build deps (needed because of no-build-isolation below)
    "setuptools", "wheel", "ninja", "packaging", "psutil", "einops",
]

# flash-attn has no wheel for torch 2.11 / sm_120: it is built from source.
# (building all 4 default archs with MAX_JOBS=8 OOM-killed nvcc on a 60GB box; sm_120 only is ~15 min.)
# Reproduce with:
#   FLASH_ATTN_CUDA_ARCHS=120 NVCC_THREADS=2 MAX_JOBS=6 CUDA_HOME=/usr/local/cuda-12.8 TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=12.0 \
#   PATH=/usr/local/cuda-12.8/bin:$PATH uv pip install flash-attn==2.8.3.post2 --no-build-isolation
# (install torch first, e.g. `uv sync --no-install-package flash-attn`, then the command above).
[tool.uv]
no-build-isolation-package = ["flash-attn"]

[tool.uv.sources]
torch = { index = "pytorch-cu128" }

[[tool.uv.index]]
name = "pytorch-cu128"
url = "https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu128"
explicit = true

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
pythonpath = ["."]
testpaths = ["tests"]
markers = ["gpu: requires a CUDA GPU"]
